title: Pouvez-vous venir ? Est-elle arrivée ?
summary: Recognise and form careful inverted questions while retaining ordinary spoken alternatives.
objectives: Form present and `passé composé` inversion with subject pronouns.
Handle linking `-t-`, reflexive pronouns and repeated noun subjects.
Recognise `puis-je`, `ai-je` and `suis-je` without overgeneralising inversion with `je`.

sources.label: Public A2 index: topic-coverage reference only

sections.title: Verb, hyphen, subject pronoun
paragraphs: Inversion places a subject pronoun after the conjugated verb, joined by a hyphen: `vous venez` → `venez-vous ?` It is common in careful questions and writing. `Est-ce que vous venez ?` and rising-intonation `vous venez ?` are also standard ways to ask, with the last especially conversational. A more formal form is not automatically a more helpful question.

With `il`, `elle` or `on`, add `-t-` between a vowel-ending verb and the pronoun: `parle-t-elle`, `va-t-on`, `a-t-il`. Do not add an extra `t` after an existing `t` or `d`: `vient-il`, `prend-elle`. The spelling remains `d` in `prend-elle` even though a `t` sound is heard.

In the `passé composé` invert the auxiliary, not the participle: `avez-vous compris`, `est-elle partie`. With reflexive verbs the reflexive pronoun remains before the verb: `vous vous levez` → `vous levez-vous`. Negative inversion puts `ne` before the pronoun/verb group and `pas` after the inverted subject: `ne vous levez-vous pas ?`
points: The `t` is a sound-linking spelling, not an apostrophe: `a-t-elle`, never `a-t'elle`.

examples.english: Does he take the same bus?
examples.note: Keep the existing `d`; do not add `-t-`.
The first `vous` is reflexive; the second is the subject.

sections.title: Noun subjects stay; `je` has restricted everyday forms
paragraphs: With a noun or name as subject, careful yes/no inversion normally keeps it before the verb and repeats it with the appropriate subject pronoun: `Léa arrive-t-elle ?` `Les dossiers sont-ils prêts ?` This is often called complex inversion; the name is not moved behind the verb.

With `je`, inversion is limited and often formal. Learn `puis-je` from `pouvoir`, `ai-je` from `avoir` and `suis-je` from `être` as useful whole forms. Do not invent `peux-je`. Questions such as `est-ce que je peux entrer ?` are natural alternatives. Many other `je` inversions sound literary or require special spelling, so use `est-ce que` rather than mechanically inverting every `je` verb.
points: In a compound tense with a name: `Léa a-t-elle répondu ?` The repeated pronoun agrees with the noun, and the auxiliary is what inverts.

examples.english: Does the centre open on Sundays?
examples.note: The noun stays and `il` repeats it.

examples.english: May I leave my bicycle here?
examples.note: A careful request; `est-ce que je peux` is less formal.

examples.french: **Ai-je** le bon numéro ? **Suis-je** au bon endroit ?
examples.english: Do I have the right number? Am I in the right place?

mistakes.why: The established inverted form of `pouvoir` with `je` is `puis-je`.

sections.title: Recognise `vais-je` without changing the following infinitive
paragraphs: `Vais-je` is another established `je` inversion. It can ask about movement or introduce a near-future action. In `vais-je devoir attendre ?`, `vais` is the conjugated word, and `devoir` and `attendre` remain infinitives. `Est-ce que je vais devoir attendre ?` gives the same question with ordinary subject order.
points: Invert the finite verb, not every verb in the chain.

examples.english: Am I heading towards the right exit?
Am I going to have to print the form?

practice.prompt: Turn Vous travaillez ici into an inverted question. Keep ici.
practice.explanation: Invert the verb and subject pronoun.

practice.prompt: Invert Elle arrive demain as a question.
Invert Tu as compris as a question.
Use the formal inversion of Je peux entrer as a question.
Invert Nous partons ensemble as a question.
Invert Ils connaissent le chemin as a question.
Invert On va au marché as a question.
Invert Elle prend le bus as a question.
Invert Tu te lèves tôt as a question.
practice.explanation: Te stays before the verb; tu moves after it.

practice.prompt: Invert Elles sont parties as a question.
Make a complex inverted question: Les magasins sont ouverts.
practice.explanation: Keep the noun and repeat it with ils.

practice.prompt: Invert Je suis en retard as a question.
Invert J'ai oublié le code as a question.
Make a complex inverted question: Nora a répondu.
practice.explanation: Keep Nora, repeat elle, invert a with linking t.

practice.prompt: Invert Vous vous reposez as a question.
practice.explanation: Reflexive vous remains before the verb.

practice.prompt: Rewrite Vous venez ? with est-ce que instead of inversion.
practice.explanation: Est-ce que allows ordinary subject-verb order.

practice.prompt: Replace est-ce que with inversion: Est-ce que je vais pouvoir récupérer mes bagages ?
practice.explanation: Invert vais-je; pouvoir and récupérer remain infinitives.

production_task.prompt: Write three clear questions to a service desk: a polite request, a question about the centre and a question about a completed action.
production_task.model_answer: Puis-je déposer mon dossier ici ? Le centre ouvre-t-il samedi ? Avez-vous reçu ma demande en ligne ?
production_task.translation: May I submit my application here? Does the centre open on Saturday? Have you received my online request?
rubric: Repeat a noun subject in complex inversion.
Invert the auxiliary in a compound tense.
